newsitem.title: USA: Germany to join IMF data release scheme - Waigel.
newsitem.headline: Germany to join IMF data release scheme - Waigel.

text.p: Germany agreed to comply with standards set by the International Monetary Fund for release of economic data at a meeting on Sunday, but details have still to be worked out, German officials said.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel said after a meeting of the International Monetary Fund's interim committee, "I said we would comply with the IMF data standard."
Germany is the last of the Group of Seven countries to join the scheme which is aimed at gathering sound economic data to improve surveillance.
The Group of Seven comprises Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States.
Germany's objection to the scheme lay in the fact that countries meeting the IMF's standards are required to state in advance when their statistics will be published.

Germany currently does not announce specific dates and times for the release of economic data in advance. Usually only a few minutes warning is given, even for highly market-sensitive data such as M3 money supply.

Asked specifically whether Germany had agreed to join the scheme only if this condition was waived, Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer told the briefing, "We have said we want to join but the technical details must still be cleared up."
Germany objects to setting precise times for publication of its data on grounds that an ambitious early release date could lead to publication of incomplete or inaccurate figures.
On the other hand, they argue, a later date which builds in a safety margin builds in a possible problem of privileged insider knowledge held by those who have access to and prepare the data.

Asked whether it would be positive or negative for financial markets to know in advance when figures were coming, Tietmeyer said, "I cannot say whether it would be positive or negative for markets to give a precise date, it is just our statistical culture."
